explanation: The answer identifies price as a factor but lacks concrete evidence that students will switch away from established delivery platforms.
strengths: Directly addresses the price point gap
weaknesses: No survey data or pilot metrics proving student willingness to switch
Fails to explain hostel batch delivery mechanics
recommended_improvement: Swiggy and Zomato are built for on-demand single orders, which results in delivery fees exceeding $1.50 per meal. NutriNest operates a hostel dorm batching model: we combine 20+ dorm orders into single scheduled delivery runs. This lowers delivery cost to $0.20 per meal, allowing us to offer fresh home-style meals at $2.50—a price point high-overhead food apps cannot match.
claims_made: Dorm batching drops delivery cost to $0.20 per meal
follow_up_question: Do you have any pilot survey data or interview results confirming students will accept scheduled batch delivery times?
